findings.title: Organization slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The organization create payload changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` into `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. That drops the negation. With billing disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is saved, so the new org has no URL. With billing enabled, `slug` is written immediately and `requestedSlug` is still written, so the slug is claimed before payment instead of staying pending. This is unrelated to destination calendars and will break org creation in both modes.

findings.title: Google Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is set
findings.body: The Cal Video fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null check. If destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], that value is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the location can be switched. The old code used optional chaining, so Meet with no Google calendar fell back to Cal Video. Every caller that passes null or [] (new bookings with no destination calendar, confirmation, and payment webhooks) will 500 on Google Meet instead of booking.

findings.title: Secondary host events are created against the first destination calendar
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent once per host credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards only credential.id into the service, not that destination's externalId. Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple all still read only the first array element: Office builds `/me/calendars/${firstExternalId}/events` with the other host's token, Lark creates on the first calendar id, and BaseCalendarService filters to the first externalId. If that id is not on the secondary account, CalDAV's filter matches nothing, Promise.all of an empty list is treated as success, and a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google does look up calendarId by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still the first destination's externalId, so the secondary Google insert can 400 or list the wrong organizer. Hosts other than the first therefore do not reliably get a calendar event, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: Team destination calendars are collected for COLLECTIVE hosts, then attached with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. The evt is initialized to null when both the event type and the organizer have no destination calendar, so the optional push is a no-op and those host calendars are discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty branch, whose fallback filters credentials with `type === "calendar"`. Real types are `google_calendar` and similar, so that fallback never matches either. A collective booking whose organizer has not set a destination calendar creates no per-host calendar events even when every other host has a calendar connected.

findings.title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host event
findings.body: The new per-reference cancel loop wraps the recurring all-remaining branch unchanged. That branch ignores the reference it is iterating, loads only booking.user.credentials (the organizer, not other hosts, and with no DB lookup), and for each future instance deletes only the first reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Other hosts' events on those instances are never deleted, so their calendars keep the cancelled series. Because this sits inside the new for-loop, the same incomplete delete also runs once per calendar reference and hammers the first event. The non-recurring branch already deletes each reference with its own credentialId and a DB fallback; the recurring branch needs the same treatment over every updated instance's calendar references.

findings.title: Payment and confirmation creates still use a single destination calendar
findings.body: Only handleNewBooking appends the other collective hosts' destination calendars. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded calls EventManager.create with an evt whose destinationCalendar is at most `[booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar]`. The same single-calendar evt is built in getBooking (used by setup_intent.succeeded around the eventManager.create call) and in paypal-webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess. confirm.handler.ts builds the same one-element list from the booking relation or the session user and passes it to handleConfirmation, without loading event-type hosts. Booking.destinationCalendar can store only the first calendar (handleNewBooking connects evt.destinationCalendar[0]). Paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings therefore still create only the organizer's calendar event, so the other hosts never get invited.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id
findings.body: updateEvent now does `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. When externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty, the find compares every calendar id to that same falsy value and always returns undefined. The previous fallback was the destination calendar's externalId. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (around line 315) uses the same dead find and then substitutes "primary", so a missing externalCalendarId deletes on the primary calendar; a 404 is treated as success and the event remains on the calendar it was actually created on. Any reference stored without externalCalendarId, including the no-credentialId create branch and seated-attendee updates that pass a null externalCalendarId, hits this.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: referencesToCreate used to set credentialId to result.credentialId for every non-calendar result. It is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video (and any other non-calendar) references are always saved without a credential id. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set, and then looks that id up in the user's credentials. New bookings will leave Zoom/Daily/other video meetings in place on cancel, and later location updates cannot find the credential that created the meeting.

findings.title: Location updates persist calendar references without ids
findings.body: updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId from result.externalId and credentialId from result.credentialId only. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field, and the previous fallbacks to evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId were removed. editLocation writes referencesToCreate onto the booking. Calendar update results have updatedEvent rather than createdEvent, so those new rows also get uid "". A later cancel treats them as legacy references and calls deleteEvent with an empty uid on every calendar credential, and the real calendar id needed to patch the existing event is gone.

findings.title: One missing host credential fails every calendar update
findings.body: The new per-reference update loop loads a credential from the DB, but if that row is missing or has no app.slug it still pushes updateEvent(undefined, ...). getCalendar then rejects. Unlike createAllCalendarEvents, there is no `if (credential)` guard. The shared catch (around line 591) also dropped the console.error, and it returns a synthetic failure for every calendar reference instead of the updates that already succeeded. With multiple host references, one deleted or unlinked credential makes reschedule, location change, and attendee updates report total calendar failure and hides the underlying error. The seated-merge delete just below also calls getCalendar on a findUnique result with no null check, so a missing old credential aborts the same way.

findings.title: CRM other_calendar references are updated twice
findings.body: calendar references are now every reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Types such as closecom_other_calendar match that filter, so they are updated in the new per-reference loop and again by the later pass that filters `type.includes("other_calendar")`. Previously find() handled only the first calendar reference, and the second pass was what updated CRM calendars. Duplicate updates can create duplicate CRM activities or fail the second call. The first loop should exclude other_calendar types.

findings.title: Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is set (rescheduling a seated attendee into an existing slot), the cleanup still does booking.references.find for a single `_calendar` reference and deletes only that event. The rest of this function was rewritten to walk every calendar reference, but this path was not. Other hosts keep a live event at the old time after the merge, so their calendars stay busy and still show the meeting.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape changed and is inconsistent
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar or null to an array or null, and that object is spread into webhook payloads. Subscribers reading destinationCalendar.integration or destinationCalendar.externalId will break, but the PR is marked as a non-breaking bug fix. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still sends null when no calendar is set, while confirm, cancel, reminders, and payment handlers send []. The e2e suite only changed BOOKING_REJECTED to expect [] and still expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED, so the new contract is neither documented nor consistently tested.

findings.title: No test covers multi-host calendar create or cancel
findings.body: This change rewrites create, update, and delete across every destination calendar, but the only test edit is an e2e webhook expectation for an empty destinationCalendar. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes one event per host credential, that Google Meet with no destination calendar still books, that Office/CalDAV/Apple hosts are not given the organizer's calendar id, or that cancelling all remaining recurring instances deletes every host event. The PR checklist notes that no such tests were added, so these regressions will not be caught before merge.
